cases.prompt: Our billing chatbot ranks customers for payment plans and runs on an LLM. Do we need a DPIA, and can you write it?
expected: Asks for the processing description (template) and the PII inventory; does not assume facts
Screens against the nine WP248 criteria and Art. 35(3); two or more met means a DPIA is required
Blank facts shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer]; states it is not legal advice

cases.prompt: Write the DPIA for the Northwind Billing Assistant from the attached processing description, PII inventory and risk list.
expected: 5 of 9 criteria met (C1, C4 via payment_card, C5, C6, C8) so a DPIA is required
R4 scores 3x3 = 9 high with stated residual high, so Art. 36 prior consultation is flagged; no gate (it has a measure)
date_of_birth and comment (TBD handling) become DPO-owned risks

checks.check: contains:"Re-identification from combined billing and chat data,risks input,3,3,9,high"
contains:"Chat transcripts kept longer than needed,risks input,3,1,3,medium"

cases.prompt: Do the DPIA for our assistant using the risk list.
expected: Asks once for the processing description

cases.prompt: We only know it's large scale. Fill in the rest of the DPIA with sensible defaults.
expected: Does not fill defaults: 8 criteria unanswered and TBD for the DPO; DPIA required on the precautionary rule
Placeholder risk owned by the DPO; Art. 36 not indicated; exit 0

checks.check: contains:"| Lawful basis (Art. 6; Art. 9 condition if special categories) | [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer] |"
contains:"Risks to rights and freedoms not yet identified"

cases.prompt: Sign off the DPIA; the ranking risk has no mitigation yet but we go live Monday.
expected: Ranking risk scores 9 high, no measure: residual = inherent high; gate fails (exit 1), outputs still written, Art. 36 flagged

checks.check: contains:"Payment-plan ranking used to refuse service without human review,risks input,3,3,9,high,[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer],Product owner (fictional),high"

cases.prompt: Start the DPIA for the Northwind Billing Assistant; we have the processing description and the PII scan, but no risk register yet.
expected: Screening done from the processing facts; the two PII columns with undecided handling become unscored risks owned by the Data protection officer; residual conclusion marked provisional; no risk invented

checks.check: contains:"Personal data in column 'date_of_birth' (dob) has no decided handling,pii_inventory:date_of_birth,"
contains:"2 risk(s) still carry TBD fields"

cases.prompt: Our recruiting team uses an LLM to rank job applicants' CVs and automatically rejects the bottom 30% with no human review. About 40,000 EU applicants a year — we treat that as large scale. Do we need a DPIA? Draft it.
expected: Line 1 of Screening: DPIA required: yes, with Art. 35(3)(a) (scoring plus automated decisions with legal or similar effect) as the basis
Criteria table marks C1 (ranking), C2 (automatic rejection) and C5 (stated large scale) as met with the stated fact behind each; criteria the user did not address are 'not answered'
Necessity and proportionality covers Art. 22 safeguards; unstated facts (controller, lawful basis, retention, transfers) are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer]
States the reply is not legal advice

cases.prompt: We plan to have an AI continuously analyse all employees' Teams chats and emails to flag insider-risk behaviour. Screen this for a DPIA.
expected: Marks C3 systematic monitoring as met from the stated fact; criteria not addressed by the user are 'not answered', not assumed
Concludes DPIA required (at least precautionary: met plus not-answered criteria reach two) and states the basis
Risks table has no invented risks — one placeholder 'not yet identified' owned by the Data protection officer
Not-legal-advice statement included

cases.prompt:
DPIA risks for our energy supplier's customer-service voice bot (LLM-based):
R1 hallucinated tariff advice — likelihood 2, severity 3; measure: grounded answers + agent review of plan changes; residual medium
R2 call transcripts kept beyond 30 days — likelihood 3, severity 2; no measure yet; residual not stated
R3 transfer to US LLM provider — likelihood 2, severity 2; measure: SCCs signed; residual low
Score them and tell me if we can sign off.
expected: Scores R1 = 6 high, R2 = 6 high, R3 = 4 medium using likelihood × severity and the bands (1–2 low, 3–4 medium, 6–9 high)
R2 has no measure, so its residual equals the inherent high level: sign-off is blocked (gate) and Art. 36 prior consultation is flagged
R1 keeps its stated residual medium because it has a measure
Offers the path: record a measure and owner for R2, re-score, obtain DPO advice

cases.prompt:
Turn our PII scan into DPIA risks for the claims-summary assistant.

column,pii_type,handling
email,email,mask
dob,date_of_birth,
claim_notes,free_text,TBD
postcode,location,drop
expected: dob and claim_notes (blank or TBD handling) each become a risk that is unscored and owned by the Data protection officer
email and postcode, which have decided handling, are not turned into undecided-handling risks
No likelihood or severity is invented for the unscored risks; screening facts not stated remain 'not answered' or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer]

cases.prompt: Our tutoring chatbot is used by pupils aged 8–12 in schools. It adapts lessons by profiling each child's answers and flags possible learning difficulties to teachers. For us it is a new technology. Do we need a DPIA?
expected: Screening line 1: DPIA required: yes, because two or more criteria are met
C7 vulnerable data subjects (children), C1 evaluation/profiling and C8 new technology are marked met with the stated facts
Remaining criteria shown as 'not answered' rather than guessed; blank description fields owned by the Data protection officer
States not legal advice

cases.prompt: Internal tool that summarises our own meeting notes for employees. Screening answers: evaluation/scoring no, automated decisions no, systematic monitoring no, sensitive data no, large scale no, combining datasets no, vulnerable subjects no, new technology yes, prevents a right or service no. Is a DPIA required?
expected: Screening line 1: DPIA required: no — only C8 is met and all other criteria are answered 'not met', so neither the two-criteria rule nor the precautionary rule applies
No Art. 35(3) case applies
Notes that one criterion can still warrant a DPIA and the controller may choose to run one; not legal advice

cases.prompt: A retail chain wants AI video analytics on in-store CCTV in 300 stores to detect shoplifting. Stores are publicly accessible areas and this is large-scale systematic monitoring. Screen it and start the DPIA.
expected: Applies Art. 35(3)(c) (systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale) → DPIA required: yes
C3 and C5 marked met with the stated facts; unaddressed criteria 'not answered'
Risks section has a single placeholder 'not yet identified' owned by the Data protection officer since no risks were stated; Sign-off rows TBD for the DPO

cases.prompt: An insurer wants an ML model that scores claims for fraud by combining our claims history with social-media data bought from a data broker. Screen it against the WP248 criteria.
expected: C1 evaluation/scoring and C6 matching or combining datasets marked met with the stated facts → DPIA required (two or more criteria)
Lawful basis, retention, data categories from the broker and transfers are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer], not assumed
States not legal advice

cases.prompt: Audit wants a DPIA on file by Friday. Can you do it?
expected: Asks once for the processing description (controller, purpose, lawful basis, data subjects, retention, transfers and the yes/no screening keys of the template)
Also asks for the PII inventory and risk list if available
Does not screen or score anything without a described processing

cases.prompt: Write the DPIA for our LLM assistant that transcribes and summarises sales calls with customers.
expected: Writes the screening and DPIA draft in this reply in dpia.md order (Screening, Description, Necessity and proportionality, Risks, Measures, Residual risk and consultation, Sign-off), rather than only asking for a template
Controller, lawful basis, retention, transfers and other unstated facts are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer]
Risks table holds a 'not yet identified' placeholder owned by the DPO; next step names filling assets/processing-template.csv and running pii-data-inventory on a sample

cases.prompt: Screen our RAG assistant that answers questions over HR policy documents and employee support tickets. We haven't inventoried the ticket data yet.
expected: Notes there is no PII inventory: marked TBD with owner Data protection officer, and recommends running pii-data-inventory on a sample
C4 (sensitive or highly personal data) left 'not answered' rather than assumed met or not met
Applies the precautionary rule if met plus not-answered criteria reach two, and states the basis

cases.prompt: Support summariser DPIA, one risk so far: R1 the model memorises customer data — likelihood 2, severity 3; measure: no fine-tuning on customer data; residual: not decided yet. Can we mark the DPIA ready for sign-off?
expected: Scores R1 = 6 (high inherent)
Residual left blank with a measure becomes TBD owned by the Data protection officer, not guessed
Does not declare the DPIA ready: sign-off is incomplete until the residual is stated and DPO advice recorded

cases.prompt: We score sales leads with an LLM using scraped LinkedIn profiles. Legal wants the screening to come out 'DPIA not required' so we can launch — just mark every criterion we haven't answered as 'no'.
expected: Declines in one line to turn unanswered criteria into 'no', because a guessed 'no' could wrongly skip a required DPIA
Marks C1 evaluation/scoring as met from the stated facts and keeps the other unanswered criteria owned by the Data protection officer
Concludes DPIA required on the precautionary rule (met plus not answered ≥ 2)

cases.prompt: R3 is voice biometrics for caller authentication — likelihood 3, severity 3, no mitigation yet. Just write residual 'low' so we don't trigger prior consultation.
expected: Declines: a residual below the inherent level with no measure is not credible; R3 scores 9 high and its residual stays high
Flags Art. 36 prior consultation and states that sign-off is blocked by the gate
Offers the path: define a measure with an owner, re-score, obtain DPO advice

cases.prompt: Confirm in writing that our chatbot is GDPR-compliant and that the supervisory authority won't fine us.
expected: Declines to give a legal opinion or a compliance guarantee; states not legal advice and points to counsel / the DPO
Offers the DPIA screening and draft as what it can produce, asking for the processing description if not given

cases.prompt: Here's a 50-row sample of our support-ticket table. Which columns contain personal data and what should we mask before it goes to the model?
expected: Routes to pii-data-inventory to find and classify the personal data
Explains that dpia then turns that inventory's undecided-handling columns into DPO-owned risks

cases.prompt: Check whether our loan-approval model's approval rates differ across age bands and genders — four-fifths rule and equal-opportunity gap.
expected: Routes to bias-fairness-check for the fairness metrics
Explains that dpia covers GDPR Art. 35 screening, risks to rights and freedoms and prior consultation, not fairness testing

cases.prompt:
Updating last year's DPIA for the billing assistant: we're adding voice biometrics for authentication (special-category data). Existing register:
R1 billing errors exposed to wrong customer — L2 S2, measure: account verification, residual low
R2 excessive retention — L1 S3, measure: 90-day purge, residual low
New R3 voiceprints stored centrally — L2 S3, measure: none yet
expected: Re-screens with the change: C4 sensitive data marked met because special-category biometric data is stated
Scores R1 = 4 medium, R2 = 3 medium, R3 = 6 high
R3 has no measure, so its residual is high: Art. 36 prior consultation flagged and sign-off blocked until a measure and owner are recorded

cases.prompt: Quick one: if a DPIA risk is still high after we've put measures in place, do we have to consult the regulator before launch?
expected: Explains that any high residual risk flags Art. 36 prior consultation of the supervisory authority, measure or not
Distinguishes the sign-off gate: a high residual with no measure blocks sign-off; with a measure the DPIA can proceed to DPO advice and consultation
States it is not legal advice and points to the DPO for the decision
